scenario: AITA for asking my pregnant SIL to leave the family Christmas gathering? | Okay so based on title I totally sound like an asshole but hear me out. So this year is our turn to host the family Christmas party at our home. We invited not only my SOs side but also my side as well. Overall it was around 20ish people in our home today for gift giving and typical American Christmas celebrating. Drinks were shared, food broken, the whole shebang. Amongst my SOs side of the family was his pregnant sister. She, I think, was due maybe a week or so ago? But really its just been ticking time bomb for her little one to arrive. Everybodys excited to meet the baby! Now our problem is that SIL came to the party with contractions and was obviously in labor (I know this because Im a mom myself - once you know, you know). Every 20 minutes or so she would start having pains and would make noises to pass the contractions. At first it wasnt so bad; I understand how sucky it is and you dont want to go to the hospital too soon because they'll just send you right home. But then it became almost obnoxious. I feel terrible for saying that but it really was. A lot of my family members and some of hers were glancing around like WTF? Go home and do that in private. After a while it became apparent that it was making everybody uncomfortable and even my MIL reccommend that she rest at home before it gets too late. She refused and said she was fine. In the middle of the kids opening their presents she went into pain again and this time she even screamed for a second. I then discreetly pulled her husband to the side and told them to leave. I did it politely ("Hey I appreciate you guys for being here but I think its time to go. I dont want you guys to give birth in our kitchen! lol"). After I said that her husband got angry and quickly got her and the kids packed up. She visibly upset and before heading out called me a bitch and said that I ruined Christmas for her. A few of their sides family members gave me dirty looks and left soon after. Im torn on this: I wanted everybody to have a good day but it was very distracting and obnoxious to have her around. I feel bad but still. tl;dr -- I asked SIL to leave family Christmas party because she was in labor.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this situation did the right thing by asking their pregnant sister-in-law (SIL) to leave the family Christmas gathering. Let me break this down step by step. First, the scenario: They're hosting a family Christmas party with around 20 people. Their SIL is pregnant, due in a week or so. She comes to the party with contractions and is clearly in labor. The person knows from experience that once you've been through labor, you can recognize the signs. So, every 20 minutes or so, she has contractions and makes noise to pass the pain. At first, it's not too bad, but it gets more disruptive over time. People start getting uncomfortable, and even the SIL's mother-in-law suggests she rest at home. She refuses, saying she's fine. Then, during the kids opening presents, she has a contraction and screams. The person pulls her husband aside and politely asks them to leave, saying they don't want them to give birth in the kitchen. The SIL gets angry, calls her a bitch, and leaves, along with some of her family members. The person feels bad but also thinks it was distracting and obnoxious. So, the question is: Was it right or wrong for the person to ask the SIL to leave? I need to consider several factors here. First, the responsibility of the host. When you host a party, you're responsible for the comfort and safety of all guests. If someone is in labor, it's a medical emergency, and the host has a duty to ensure that the situation is handled appropriately. Allowing someone in active labor to stay in a crowded home could be dangerous if complications arise. It's also disruptive to the party, which was meant to be a joyful occasion. Another point is the comfort of the other guests. When the SIL started having more intense contractions and screaming, it made the environment uncomfortable for everyone. Children were present, and having a woman scream in pain during their gift-opening could be traumatic or at least unsettling. The host has to balance the needs of all guests, not just the SIL. Additionally, the SIL's refusal to leave despite being advised by her mother-in-law and the host could be seen as irresponsible. She was putting herself and possibly her baby at risk by not seeking proper medical attention. The host's suggestion to leave was a way to ensure she gets the care she needs, even if it was delivered in a polite manner. On the flip side, the SIL was attending the party and had a right to be there. She might have felt that she was managing her contractions and didn't want to miss out on the celebration. The host's decision to ask her to leave could have been perceived as insensitive, especially since the SIL was in a vulnerable state. However, the host's primary responsibility is to the safety and comfort of all attendees. Given that the SIL was in active labor, it was reasonable to suggest she leave to go to the hospital. The host's approach was polite, which is commendable, but the SIL's reaction was emotional and perhaps not entirely rational given the circumstances. In conclusion, while the host's decision may have caused some hurt feelings, it was the responsible choice to ensure the safety of the SIL and the comfort of the other guests. It's a tough situation, but in the end, the host acted appropriately under the circumstances.
